findings.finding: The public statement quantifies over natural dimensions d >= 2, real 0 < B <= 2d, and 0 <= beta_0 < B; it chooses a finite nonnegative real C before g, N >= 2 and beta in [0,beta_0]. This is the approved uniform conditional assertion, including beta=0. The natural subtraction in 2^(d-1) agrees with the intended exponent on d >= 2. No endpoint beta=B or range B>2d is claimed.

Fin d -> AddCircle 1 with product normalized Haar is the unit torus with probability measure. Fourier characters have the negative exponent convention; latticeNorm is Euclidean. The zero coefficient is zero and nonzero coefficients are exactly 2^(d-1) pi^(d/2) Gamma(d/2)/(2 pi |k|)^d. The partition exponent is +beta/(2N) times the ordered distinct-pair sum. No volume, factor-of-two, or sign mismatch was found.

FiniteEntropyDensity requires a measurable real representative, nonnegativity almost everywhere, integral one, integrability of rho and of rho log rho. On a probability space, the lower bound t log t >= -1/e for t >= 0 makes integrability of rho log rho the usual finite-entropy condition. Lean totalization at log 0 is harmless because rho log rho=0 there; arbitrary negative values on a null set are harmless. Absolutely continuous finite-entropy probability measures admit representatives of this kind. The measure-to-density correspondence is a mathematical interpretation here, not a separately certified public bridge theorem.

LogHLSWithDomain universally demands absolute integrability of the full centered interaction integrand for every finite-entropy density, and the log-HLS inequality for that same density. It is not restricted to densities whose energy happened to be integrable. Thus the public theorem avoids interpreting a nonintegrable Bochner energy as zero. The original LogHLS-only result is retained as a distinct stronger implication with a weaker antecedent; main_with_domain correctly discards the integrability conjunct to invoke it.

The partition is a nonnegative extended integral in ENNReal of a measurable exponential weight, so a divergent partition is top, not zero. Its comparison with a coerced NNReal constant asserts actual finiteness. The integral is over N independent uniform particles. The real-valued representative at collisions does not change the integral because the diagonal is null for this Haar measure in d >= 2.

findings.topic: A.e. representatives and uniformity over kernels
findings.finding: Integrable kernels with the fixed coefficients agree almost everywhere by ae_eq_of_coeff_eq. Off-diagonal pair differences preserve Haar-null sets under independent sampling; partition_congr_ae transfers equality to the partition. Paper.paper_main actually uses these results to select C before all representatives. No pointwise evenness or a fixed diagonal value is silently required in the public target.

kernel_exists produces a measurable integrable real kernel with the prescribed Fourier coefficients for each d >= 2. It does not produce B or prove LogHLSWithDomain for that kernel. Paper.paper_main explicitly permits the vacuous case in which no normalized kernel satisfies the LogHLS assumption at the selected B. This is valid for the approved conditional scope but cannot substantiate an unconditional partition bound or nonempty admissible positive-coupling range. The finite-entropy density class itself is nonempty (rho=1).

IsLogKernel uses Fourier coefficients and L1 integrability, not a local logarithmic estimate. LogAsymptotic is only a definition and does not occur in the public conclusion. The short draft states a local -log|x|+O(1) property, while this release deliberately uses the Fourier characterization. Neither existence nor the public partition theorem should be described as separately certifying that local asymptotic.

findings.topic: Short draft versus canonical Part I
findings.finding: The short draft theorem is the conditional uniform partition bound. The canonical Part I principal theorem also asserts threshold identity, determinant convergence with O(1/N) error, positive pressure, fixed-particle sharp integrability, and transported-reference results. Its functional-domain section supplies a finite-entropy energy argument and derives the macroscopic inequality from beta_gm. Those claims and bridges are outside the reviewed public Lean target. The approved public result is a conditional ingredient of canonical Part I, not certification of its full principal theorem or all Part I.

The ambient Pi metric on Fin d -> AddCircle 1 is the maximum coordinate distance, whereas the defined radius is the Euclidean combination of circle distances. TorusBase proves dist <= radius <= sqrt(d)*dist; latticeNorm independently uses the Euclidean norm. The public theorem and its Fourier normalization do not use the ambient metric, and no exact local-asymptotic conclusion is advertised, so the distinction is not a defect in the approved statement.

Direct text comparisons after stripping introductory comments found the frozen mathematical declaration prefix in PaperSolution identical to PaperChallenge, and the PaperTheoremWithDomain declaration identical in the domain challenge and solution. The proof library uses corresponding torus, density, Fourier coefficient, energy and partition definitions; the public aliases main and kernel_exists expose the intended statements. Kernel checking/type equality is a separate verification obligation.

The frozen specification commentary says the kernel is not constructed, uniqueness is unavailable in Mathlib, and that existence is not proved here. As a statement-only file this is historical context, but copied verbatim into PaperSolution these remarks can mislead readers about the current proof library, which proves Fourier uniqueness and kernel existence. The phrase Theorem 1.1 as stated in the paper must be tied to the short draft, not read as the current canonical principal theorem. Contextualize these comments in public scope documentation without modifying the frozen target.
